bull_bear.body: Prioritizing reinvestment for growth (brand building, capacity, working capital). Maintaining ~15% dividend payout. No buybacks planned; cash held in FDs/Liquid funds to support expansion and cover INR 95cr carpenter bonus liability.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Working Capital: Receivable days stretched to 150-160 days (vs normal 120) due to new state entry; Raw Materials: VAM price volatility linked to crude/geopolitics; Competition: New capacity additions by peers in Gujarat; Demand: Potential short-term demand destruction from sharp price hikes, though management sees limited impact as adhesives are small % of total furniture cost.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Optimistic and aggressive on market share capture; transparent about working capital stretch being a strategic choice for new market entry; confident in passing on raw material costs; focused on 'transformation journey' from distributor-led to brand-led model.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'carpenter bonus liability' of ~INR 95cr acts as a unique working capital feature, effectively an interest-free float from the channel that funds part of the cash balance. The company is deliberately stretching receivables in new states for 2-3 years to build relationships, accepting lower cash conversion temporarily for market share.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Guidance to maintain 30-40%+ ROE and 40%+ ROCE; FY25 delivered 35%+ ROE and ~50%+ ROCE.
- Company remains debt-free, net debt negative since FY18, and continues to generate positive operating and free cash flows.
- FY25 final dividend of 90% dividend per share, with a 15% dividend payout ratio for FY25.
- Targets keeping liabilities for expenses below 30-35% of revenue (~34% in FY25).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Brand position: over twenty years EURO 7000 has become the second-largest selling wood-adhesive retail brand in India, with an estimated 15-35% share in its strongest states.
- Distribution depth: roughly 12,000 dealers and over 520 sales and business development executives, with in-shop branding at 5,000+ retail counters and revamped displays at more than 2,500 counters.
- Carpenter loyalty moat: a state-wise loyalty programme with a digital app for earning, claiming and redeeming points, built on relationships with a large registered-carpenter base.
- Competes on product performance and channel service rather than price, per the MD&A.
- Debt-free balance sheet since FY 2017-18, funding capacity, brand and channel investment from internal accruals.
- Regulatory tailwind favouring its water-borne PVA chemistry from the BIS formaldehyde-emission norms in force from February 2025.
- Headroom in its own footprint: of the 14 states of operation only about five are mature, with the top five still contributing ~75-80% of volumes.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw-material volatility and full import dependence on vinyl acetate monomer (VAM) — VAM is about 90% of raw-material cost and is fully imported with no domestic manufacture, so input prices and currency movements pass straight into gross margin; the MD&A grades this first among ten principal risks and mitigates it with multi-vendor sourcing, calibrated pricing and low inventory. The forward-looking-statement caveat also names raw-material prices and availability, and currency movements, among factors beyond the Company's control.
- Single-site concentration at Santej — All manufacturing sits at the single Santej site, so any disruption there stops supply nationally. Mitigation cited is maintenance, insurance and planned capacity; the Company also carries an Industrial All Risk policy on plant, property, equipment and stocks.
- Product and category concentration in white glue — The Company operates in a single reportable segment of synthetic wood adhesives and describes itself as focused on its main product, white glue, so there is no second category to absorb a demand or technology shift. Mitigation cited is premiumisation within the EURO 7000 family and adjacencies assessed against return criteria.
- Channel and scheme dependence — Sales run through roughly 12,000 dealers and a carpenter loyalty scheme, so volumes depend on continued dealer and carpenter participation and on the economics of the reward slabs. Mitigation cited is a diversified dealer base and direct carpenter engagement.
- Credit risk on an extended receivables cycle — Trade receivables ran at 185 days on a closing basis, described as a design feature of the carpenter-loyalty scheme cycle rather than distress, with bad debts of 0.36% of revenue. Mitigation cited is credit limits, ageing review and Ind AS 109 expected-credit-loss provisioning; debtors' turnover fell to 2.21x from 2.60x on scheme-cycle and new-market credit.
- Competitive intensity in a category led by one dominant national player — The category is led by a single large player with other smaller players, leaving the Company second; it competes on product performance and channel service rather than price, and management separately flags a marketplace reality of discount-driven sales pushes and brand clutter. Mitigation cited is brand equity and service.
- Key-person dependence — The business is run by a small executive team, and the MD&A lists key-person dependence among its ten principal risks, mitigated through second-line building and succession planning via the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.
- Treasury and market risk on a large cash pile — Rs.165.93 crore of surpluses - 39% of assets, including about Rs.46.8 crore in liquid funds - sits undeployed and is exposed to market risk; it is governed by a Board investment policy with quarterly Audit-Committee review. Retained cash awaiting deployment is also cited as the principal cause of the fall in return on net worth.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Retail contributes ~94% of revenue; OEM segment currently ~6% with target to reach 15% in 2-3 years. Geographic mix shifting from Gujarat/Maharashtra stronghold to new states (UP, Delhi, WB, Odisha, Chhattisgarh).

latest_quarter.body: Gross Margin target 65%; EBITDA target 23-25%. Pressure from VAM prices doubling (INR 75-80 to INR 160-180/kg); management passed through 60-70% of cost hike via price increases effective May 1st. Advertising intensity increasing from 4% to 6-7% of revenue.

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 15-20% volume CAGR targeted for next 2-3 years to reach INR 500cr; Margin: Sustainable EBITDA band of 23-25% (Gross Margin ~65%); Order Inflow: Focus on tertiary offtake via carpenter engagement; Capex: Brownfield expansion completing in 1-2 quarters (capacity 2,000 -> 3,500 tons/month).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not applicable for B2C adhesive model; performance tracked via monthly volume run-rates (March hit >2,100 tons).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Untapped market share in mature states (only ~1/3 retail outlets penetrated in Mumbai); expansion into 2 new states in May '26; OEM segment scaling in metro cities; long-term vision to reach INR 1,000-1,200cr revenue.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Singular focus on the white-glue business rather than diversification, investing to enhance capability and expand reach in existing and new states.
- Invest deliberately behind the 'EURO 7000 Wood Adhesive' brand and the distribution that carries it - stepped-up advertising and trade support, and a nationwide campaign with brand ambassador Mr. Pankaj Tripathi.
- Deepen penetration in the existing 14+ states, where only about five are mature and the top five still contribute ~75-80% of volumes, while steadily evaluating and entering new states.
- Premiumisation within the EURO 7000 family and adding adjacent SKUs on the existing dealer network, with return criteria applied to adjacencies.
- Carpenter Loyalty Program run through a dedicated app with a clear slab-based points system, backed by state-wise programmes and 54 dealer meets during the year, as the core channel-engagement engine.
- Strategic sourcing and stronger vendor relationships to secure material procurement cost efficiencies while holding quality standards.
- Maintain financial stability and flexibility - a debt-free status and robust operating cash flows - with capacity, brand and channel investment funded from internal accruals.
- Scale capacity ahead of demand - production capacity scaled up to 40,000 tons per annum, with a dedicated warehouse facility being established for raw materials and finished goods.
- Board approved, in June 2026 and subject to necessary approvals, a direct listing of the Company's shares on the National Stock Exchange, to widen ownership and visibility.
- Report to shareholders each quarter on three measures: the pace and volume-basis of revenue growth, the trajectory of receivables, and the margin band.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company operates from a single manufacturing unit at Santej (Gandhinagar, Gujarat), originally set up in 1994-95 over about 8,000 square yards. Capacity has been raised in steps - to 500 TPM in 2016-17, to 1,000 TPM in 2018-19, doubled to 2,000 TPM in 2022 - and the Corporate Overview states manufacturing capacity of 40,000 TPA with capacity growth of 2x in the last 2-3 years. Management says that in response to increasing demand and to strengthen market share it has successfully scaled up production capacity to 40,000 tons per annum, and is additionally establishing a dedicated warehouse facility to optimise storage of both raw materials and finished goods (a process the milestone timeline shows was initiated in 2022). Looking forward, the MD&A's Opportunities section states that a brownfield addition of about 1,500 tonnes per month and a greenfield project of about Rs.45 crore are planned; the Outlook section says the medium-term revenue ambition is supported by this planned brownfield and greenfield capacity. No commissioning date, location or ramp timeline is given for either project. Funding is described as coming from a debt-free balance sheet and internal accruals, with the MD&A citing Rs.165.93 crore of internal resources and noting that returns were diluted by retained cash awaiting deployment. Single-site concentration at Santej is itself listed as a principal risk, mitigated in part by 'planned capacity'. The Board's Report records that the Company undertook no mergers, amalgamations, acquisitions, takeovers or restructuring transactions during the year and has no subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures, so no capacity or geography was added inorganically.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Macro tailwind: India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with manufacturing up 10.7% and construction firm - a direct tailwind for housing, interiors and furniture; RBI projects 6.6% GDP growth for FY 2026-27.
- A 100 bps repo-rate cut during the year to 5.25% (December 2025), since held, is described as supporting renovation demand.
- Category demand driven by housing and affordable-housing programmes, the modular-furniture boom and formalisation of the plywood/MDF chain.
- BIS formaldehyde-emission norms in force from February 2025 are described as a regulatory tailwind favouring the Company's water-borne PVA chemistry.
- India's adhesives and sealants market is estimated at USD 2.3-3.4 billion in 2025 growing ~6-11% p.a., with the wood-adhesives sub-segment at ~USD 414 million by 2030 (~7.2% CAGR, Grand View Research).
- Structural runway inside the existing footprint: only about five of 14 states are mature and the top five still contribute ~75-80% of volumes.
- Exit velocity: a soft first quarter gave way to a fourth quarter up 18.2% year-on-year, which management calls the exit velocity into FY 2026-27.
- Margin lever: gross margin improved ~119 bps to ~70.2%, with the margin decline attributed to deliberate brand and channel spend (employee, sales promotion, commission and other expenses) rather than pricing.
- Category structure: led by one dominant national player, with the Company competing on product performance and channel service rather than price, holding an estimated 15-35% share in its strongest states.
- Threats flagged: raw-material volatility and full import dependence on vinyl acetate monomer (~90% of raw-material cost), single-site concentration at Santej, category concentration in white glue, channel and scheme dependence, credit risk on the extended receivables cycle, and competitive intensity.
- Retained cash awaiting deployment, not operating deterioration, is cited as the principal cause of the return-on-net-worth dilution, with pre-tax return on capital employed described as remaining ~36.5%.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Jyoti Resins delivered record Q4 revenue (+18% YoY) driven by 16% volume growth and aggressive brand spending, signaling a shift from pure distribution to brand-led market share capture. However, rising receivables (150-160 days) and a 100% spike in key raw material (VAM) prices pose near-term margin and cash flow risks despite 60-70% price pass-through initiated in May.

risks.risk: Raw-material volatility and full import dependence on vinyl acetate monomer (VAM)
risks.note: VAM is about 90% of raw-material cost and is fully imported with no domestic manufacture, so input prices and currency movements pass straight into gross margin; the MD&A grades this first among ten principal risks and mitigates it with multi-vendor sourcing, calibrated pricing and low inventory. The forward-looking-statement caveat also names raw-material prices and availability, and currency movements, among factors beyond the Company's control.

All manufacturing sits at the single Santej site, so any disruption there stops supply nationally. Mitigation cited is maintenance, insurance and planned capacity; the Company also carries an Industrial All Risk policy on plant, property, equipment and stocks.

risks.risk: Product and category concentration in white glue
risks.note: The Company operates in a single reportable segment of synthetic wood adhesives and describes itself as focused on its main product, white glue, so there is no second category to absorb a demand or technology shift. Mitigation cited is premiumisation within the EURO 7000 family and adjacencies assessed against return criteria.

Sales run through roughly 12,000 dealers and a carpenter loyalty scheme, so volumes depend on continued dealer and carpenter participation and on the economics of the reward slabs. Mitigation cited is a diversified dealer base and direct carpenter engagement.

risks.risk: Credit risk on an extended receivables cycle
risks.note: Trade receivables ran at 185 days on a closing basis, described as a design feature of the carpenter-loyalty scheme cycle rather than distress, with bad debts of 0.36% of revenue. Mitigation cited is credit limits, ageing review and Ind AS 109 expected-credit-loss provisioning; debtors' turnover fell to 2.21x from 2.60x on scheme-cycle and new-market credit.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity in a category led by one dominant national player
risks.note: The category is led by a single large player with other smaller players, leaving the Company second; it competes on product performance and channel service rather than price, and management separately flags a marketplace reality of discount-driven sales pushes and brand clutter. Mitigation cited is brand equity and service.

The business is run by a small executive team, and the MD&A lists key-person dependence among its ten principal risks, mitigated through second-line building and succession planning via the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.

risks.risk: Treasury and market risk on a large cash pile
risks.note: Rs.165.93 crore of surpluses - 39% of assets, including about Rs.46.8 crore in liquid funds - sits undeployed and is exposed to market risk; it is governed by a Board investment policy with quarterly Audit-Committee review. Retained cash awaiting deployment is also cited as the principal cause of the fall in return on net worth.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jyoti Resins and Adhesives Limited is a single-site Gujarat wood-adhesive maker whose EURO 7000 white glue is described as the second-largest selling wood-adhesive retail brand in India, sold across 14 states.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1994, the Company manufactures synthetic wood adhesives and allied products at Santej (Gandhinagar, Gujarat) and sells them under the 'Euro 7000' brand launched in 2006. It operates in a single reportable segment under Ind AS 108, reaching the market through a retail channel of roughly 12,000 dealers and a large registered-carpenter network across 14 states. Alongside the retail white-glue range it sells an industrial EWR line aimed at furniture manufacturers.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Retail contributes ~94% of revenue; OEM segment currently ~6% with target to reach 15% in 2-3 years. Geographic mix shifting from Gujarat/Maharashtra stronghold to new states (UP, Delhi, WB, Odisha, Chhattisgarh).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Retail wood adhesives:** EURO 7000 white glue, EURO 7000 XTRA, EURO 7000 WP 2-in-1, EURO 7000 Extreme 3, EURO 7000 Ultra 5-in-1, PVC Glue
- **Industrial adhesives (Euro EWR range):** EWR Eco Grade, EWR Max, EWR E3+

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Retail carpenters, contractors and woodworking professionals
- Furniture manufacturing and the modular-furniture segment
- Housing, renovation and interiors demand
- Plywood / MDF value chain
- Large institutions served through direct commercial engagement
- 14 states in India, including Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana, Punjab and Himachal Pradesh

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable for B2C adhesive model; performance tracked via monthly volume run-rates (March hit >2,100 tons).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 15-20% volume CAGR targeted for next 2-3 years to reach INR 500cr; Margin: Sustainable EBITDA band of 23-25% (Gross Margin ~65%); Order Inflow: Focus on tertiary offtake via carpenter engagement; Capex: Brownfield expansion completing in 1-2 quarters (capacity 2,000 -> 3,500 tons/month).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Untapped market share in mature states (only ~1/3 retail outlets penetrated in Mumbai); expansion into 2 new states in May '26; OEM segment scaling in metro cities; long-term vision to reach INR 1,000-1,200cr revenue.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Macro tailwind: India's real GDP grew 7.7% in FY 2025-26 with manufacturing up 10.7% and construction firm - a direct tailwind for housing, interiors and furniture; RBI projects 6.6% GDP growth for FY 2026-27.
- A 100 bps repo-rate cut during the year to 5.25% (December 2025), since held, is described as supporting renovation demand.
- Category demand driven by housing and affordable-housing programmes, the modular-furniture boom and formalisation of the plywood/MDF chain.
- BIS formaldehyde-emission norms in force from February 2025 are described as a regulatory tailwind favouring the Company's water-borne PVA chemistry.
- India's adhesives and sealants market is estimated at USD 2.3-3.4 billion in 2025 growing ~6-11% p.a., with the wood-adhesives sub-segment at ~USD 414 million by 2030 (~7.2% CAGR, Grand View Research).
- Structural runway inside the existing footprint: only about five of 14 states are mature and the top five still contribute ~75-80% of volumes.
- Exit velocity: a soft first quarter gave way to a fourth quarter up 18.2% year-on-year, which management calls the exit velocity into FY 2026-27.
- Margin lever: gross margin improved ~119 bps to ~70.2%, with the margin decline attributed to deliberate brand and channel spend (employee, sales promotion, commission and other expenses) rather than pricing.
- Category structure: led by one dominant national player, with the Company competing on product performance and channel service rather than price, holding an estimated 15-35% share in its strongest states.
- Threats flagged: raw-material volatility and full import dependence on vinyl acetate monomer (~90% of raw-material cost), single-site concentration at Santej, category concentration in white glue, channel and scheme dependence, credit risk on the extended receivables cycle, and competitive intensity.
- Retained cash awaiting deployment, not operating deterioration, is cited as the principal cause of the return-on-net-worth dilution, with pre-tax return on capital employed described as remaining ~36.5%.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross Margin target 65%; EBITDA target 23-25%. Pressure from VAM prices doubling (INR 75-80 to INR 160-180/kg); management passed through 60-70% of cost hike via price increases effective May 1st. Advertising intensity increasing from 4% to 6-7% of revenue.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing reinvestment for growth (brand building, capacity, working capital). Maintaining ~15% dividend payout. No buybacks planned; cash held in FDs/Liquid funds to support expansion and cover INR 95cr carpenter bonus liability.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company operates from a single manufacturing unit at Santej (Gandhinagar, Gujarat), originally set up in 1994-95 over about 8,000 square yards. Capacity has been raised in steps - to 500 TPM in 2016-17, to 1,000 TPM in 2018-19, doubled to 2,000 TPM in 2022 - and the Corporate Overview states manufacturing capacity of 40,000 TPA with capacity growth of 2x in the last 2-3 years. Management says that in response to increasing demand and to strengthen market share it has successfully scaled up production capacity to 40,000 tons per annum, and is additionally establishing a dedicated warehouse facility to optimise storage of both raw materials and finished goods (a process the milestone timeline shows was initiated in 2022). Looking forward, the MD&A's Opportunities section states that a brownfield addition of about 1,500 tonnes per month and a greenfield project of about Rs.45 crore are planned; the Outlook section says the medium-term revenue ambition is supported by this planned brownfield and greenfield capacity. No commissioning date, location or ramp timeline is given for either project. Funding is described as coming from a debt-free balance sheet and internal accruals, with the MD&A citing Rs.165.93 crore of internal resources and noting that returns were diluted by retained cash awaiting deployment. Single-site concentration at Santej is itself listed as a principal risk, mitigated in part by 'planned capacity'. The Board's Report records that the Company undertook no mergers, amalgamations, acquisitions, takeovers or restructuring transactions during the year and has no subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures, so no capacity or geography was added inorganically.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Optimistic and aggressive on market share capture; transparent about working capital stretch being a strategic choice for new market entry; confident in passing on raw material costs; focused on 'transformation journey' from distributor-led to brand-led model.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Brand position: over twenty years EURO 7000 has become the second-largest selling wood-adhesive retail brand in India, with an estimated 15-35% share in its strongest states.
- Distribution depth: roughly 12,000 dealers and over 520 sales and business development executives, with in-shop branding at 5,000+ retail counters and revamped displays at more than 2,500 counters.
- Carpenter loyalty moat: a state-wise loyalty programme with a digital app for earning, claiming and redeeming points, built on relationships with a large registered-carpenter base.
- Competes on product performance and channel service rather than price, per the MD&A.
- Debt-free balance sheet since FY 2017-18, funding capacity, brand and channel investment from internal accruals.
- Regulatory tailwind favouring its water-borne PVA chemistry from the BIS formaldehyde-emission norms in force from February 2025.
- Headroom in its own footprint: of the 14 states of operation only about five are mature, with the top five still contributing ~75-80% of volumes.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Working Capital: Receivable days stretched to 150-160 days (vs normal 120) due to new state entry; Raw Materials: VAM price volatility linked to crude/geopolitics; Competition: New capacity additions by peers in Gujarat; Demand: Potential short-term demand destruction from sharp price hikes, though management sees limited impact as adhesives are small % of total furniture cost.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The 'carpenter bonus liability' of ~INR 95cr acts as a unique working capital feature, effectively an interest-free float from the channel that funds part of the cash balance. The company is deliberately stretching receivables in new states for 2-3 years to build relationships, accepting lower cash conversion temporarily for market share.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Singular focus on the white-glue business rather than diversification, investing to enhance capability and expand reach in existing and new states.
- Invest deliberately behind the 'EURO 7000 Wood Adhesive' brand and the distribution that carries it - stepped-up advertising and trade support, and a nationwide campaign with brand ambassador Mr. Pankaj Tripathi.
- Deepen penetration in the existing 14+ states, where only about five are mature and the top five still contribute ~75-80% of volumes, while steadily evaluating and entering new states.
